candidates.angle: tyagam, the word for giving up, and what it really means here
Krishna calls fear-based quitting a form of passionate action
The verse distinguishes between abandoning action and the fruit of letting go

angle_en: Rajasa tyaga: the passionate giving up

en.intro: Krishna has been sorting the different kinds of giving up. Listen to the one that looks like peace but is actually fear.
en.notice: Krishna calls this kind of giving up rajasa, passionate. It is not the calm of true release, but the restless recoil of someone who steps back from their duty simply because it hurts.
en.next: Krishna now turns to the giving up that is done without clinging to results, the true sattvic path.
en.meaning: If someone gives up action thinking it is only suffering and fearing bodily strain, that renunciation is passionate, and it brings no fruit of renunciation.

hi.intro: कृष्ण त्याग के विभिन्न प्रकारों को समझा रहे हैं। उस त्याग को सुनिए जो शांति जैसा लगता है, लेकिन असल में डर है।
hi.meaning: जो कुछ कर्म है, वह दुःखरूप ही है ऐसा समझकर कोई शारीरिक क्लेशके भयसे उसका त्याग कर दे, तो वह राजस त्याग करके भी त्यागके फलको नहीं पाता।
hi.next: कृष्ण अब उस त्याग की ओर मुड़ते हैं जो बिना किसी फल की आसक्ति के किया जाता है, वही सात्त्विक त्याग कहलाता है।

en.intro: Krishna has been sorting the different kinds of giving up. Listen to the one that looks like peace but is actually fear.
en.body: If someone gives up action thinking it is only suffering and fearing bodily strain, that renunciation is passionate, and it brings no fruit of renunciation. Krishna calls this kind of giving up rajasa, passionate. It is not the calm of true release, but the restless recoil of someone who steps back from their duty simply because it hurts. Krishna now turns to the giving up that is done without clinging to results, the true sattvic path.

issues: meaning_changed: "कृष्ण इसे राजस त्याग कहते हैं, भावुक त्याग" (The source identifies the type of renunciation as 'rajasic' (राजसं), which means passionate or driven by restless energy, not 'भावुक' (emotional/sentimental). The Hindi translation adds an emotional connotation that contradicts the specific philosophical term used in the source.)

borrowed: "Notice: कृष्ण इसे राजस त्याग कहते हैं, जो बेचैन ऊर्जा से प्रेरित है। यह शांतिपूर्ण त्याग नहीं है, बल्कि कर्तव्य से भागने का बेचैन प्रयास है जो केवल शारीरिक कष्ट के डर से किया जाता है।" (The notice describes the giving up as 'restless energy' (bechain oorja) and 'restless effort' (bechain prayas). This is a characterization/interpretation not strictly present in the source text (which uses 'rajasa' - passionate) and borrows the conceptual framing of the NEXT verse (sattvic path) as a contrast, misattributing the 'restlessness' template to this specific verse's notice.)
